title: Testing the new Tavelo grow in a UCI gravel race!

takeaways.text: Tavelo rates 55 mm front and 50 mm rear; his 45 mm tires measured about 48 mm on 32 mm-internal Tavelo wheels with plenty of room left. He fitted a 56T chainring for a fast race, above the 50T figure others cite, without reported rub.

The fork steerer is eccentric; Tavelo told him it slims the head tube around the internal routing and improves the fork angle for steering. The stock bar is 40 cm at the hoods flaring to 46.5 cm in the drops.
In a 144 km UCI race averaging 39.6 km/h it felt light, reactive and aero; the stock-style bottle cages ejected both bottles early, which he blamed on the cages and replaced.
After a further 180 km gravel ride: road-like and aggressive on the hoods, very controlled in the flared drops, and quick in corners.
His SRAM Rival AXS build weighed about 8.44 kg; he quotes US$1,899 retail for frame plus bar and US$1,000 for the wheels.

disclosure: Race test by a former WorldTour road professional; he discussed the frame with Tavelo's co-founder, but how the bike was obtained is not stated in the video.
summary: Former road pro builds a Tavelo Grow with SRAM Rival 1× and races it in a 144 km Belgian UCI gravel event, then on a 180 km endurance ride.
